R was built around statistical computing and graphics, which makes it unusually expressive for exploratory analysis and statistical modeling.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key ideas
`vector` `data.frame` `factor` `NA` `function` `formula`
`subset` `apply` `package` `plot` `ggplot2`
:::

## Start with the vector

```r
x <- c(8, 11, 7, 14, 10)

mean(x)
sd(x)
x[x > 10]
```

Much of R becomes easier once you think in **vectors rather than row-by-row loops**.

## Learn in this order

```text
vectors + types
 ↓
data frames
 ↓
indexing
 ↓
functions
 ↓
missing values
 ↓
visualization
 ↓
packages
 ↓
statistical models
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Base R and tidyverse are not enemies
Learn enough **base R** to read ordinary R code and understand vectors/functions. Learn **tidyverse** tools because they provide a coherent workflow for transformation, visualization and modern data analysis.
:::
